comments.text: I was in a folk dance class in my freshman year of college and we were doing a Russian dance where part of the choreography was to run backwards. Well, we were misaligned and I slammed into a guy who was shorter than me. He hit the top of his head, and I hit the back of my skull, hard. He walked away with a superficial injury, I walked away with a concussion that changed the course of my life. It was diagnosed as mild, but that wasn't actually the case. We later found out it was moderate to severe and I lost the ability to read more than a few sentences, focus, recall information (like words when I was speaking), and it triggered Fibromyalgia in my body. So I became disabled. I did manage to graduate college 10 years later with a lot of effort and support from the accessibility center and my Professors. I'm glad Salish wasn't severely injured by her run in with her classmate. I know firsthand that that can be an incredibly dangerous sort of accident.

I spend a lot of time around horses, at the fields or at the yard. Luckily I never needed to remember about chest compositions, but.. 
ICE ICE, BABY is my emergency protocol. Vast majority  of minor injuries like a bump, if you cold hose it immediately, you will be better for it. Recently I got kicked by a horse on top front of the thigh, horse wasn't shod luckily. Wellies off, leggings off, leg under the hose. Ice pack, vet wrap, finish horses, home, leg up ice bandage. Bruise showed up on almost half of the thigh. I have dodgy connective tissues, so I was expecting it to be worse. It healed in a week! Not that I'm doing a little victory dance 😂💃🏼 impressive recovery. 
That little trick saved me some serious consequences many times.
